title: Zero-dimensional smooth fibre point admits a singleton-fibre etale open
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $x\in X$, and put $s=f(x)$. Assume there is an open subscheme $W\subseteq X$ containing $x$ [def-weil-open-immersion] for which $f|_W:W\to S$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Assume that $\dim_x(X_s)=0$, where $X_s$ is the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and dimension at a point means the minimum of the dimensions of its open neighbourhoods [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. Then there exists an open subscheme $Z\subseteq W$ containing $x$ such that $f|_Z:Z\to S$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and $Z_s$ has underlying set $\{x\}$, with $x$ viewed as the corresponding point of $Z_s$. The inclusion $Z\to X$ is an immersion (a closed immersion followed by an open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]). No closed-point or separability hypothesis is imposed on $x$.

source.place: Tag 057G, lemma-slice-smooth, proof: entire paragraph headed "The case d = 0", including the final open restriction making the fibre a singleton; fibre topology from Tag 01K1, lemma-fibre-topological (schemes.tex).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-near-point-smooth-zero-fibre-dimension] to $f$, $x$ and the given $W$. Its smoothness and zero fibre-dimension hypotheses are exactly ours. We obtain an open $U\subseteq W$ containing $x$ with $g=f|_U:U\to S$ etale.

source.place: Tag 057G, lemma-slice-smooth, proof, case d = 0: shrinking to an etale open; the existing cited criterion supplies this shrinking.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points], $|U_s|$ is discrete, so the singleton of the point above $x$ is open. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre], the fibre projection identifies $|U_s|$ homeomorphically with the subspace $g^{-1}(s)\subseteq |U|$. Consequently $\{x\}$ is open in that subspace. By the definition of subspace topology [def-kun-subspace-topology] there is an open $V\subseteq |U|$ with $V\cap g^{-1}(s)=\{x\}$. In particular $x\in V$.

source.place: Tag 02GL, lemma-etale-over-field (2); schemes.tex Tag 01K1, lemma-fibre-topological; applied as in Tag 057G, d = 0.

proof.text: Let $Z$ be the open subscheme of $U$ defined by $V$. Open subsets of an open subspace are open in the ambient space; restriction of $\mathcal O_X$ first to $U$ and then to $V$ is its restriction to $V$. Thus [def-weil-open-immersion] identifies $Z$ with an open subscheme of $X$ contained in $U\subseteq W$. Applying [def-pc-scheme-fibre] to $f|_Z$ identifies $|Z_s|$ with $V\cap g^{-1}(s)=\{x\}$. The inclusion $Z\to U$ is open, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] makes it etale and makes its composite with $g$ etale. This composite is $f|_Z$.

source.place: Tag 057G, lemma-slice-smooth, proof, case d = 0, final open restriction; morphisms.tex Tags 02GP and 02GN.

proof.text: The inclusion $Z\to X$ is an immersion in the stated sense [def-weil-closed-immersion]: factor it as the identity $Z\to Z$ followed by its open inclusion in $X$. The identity is a closed immersion because its underlying image is all of $Z$ and its structure-sheaf map is the identity, hence surjective. No step used closedness of $x$ in $X$ or a hypothesis on its residue extension.

proof_origin.place: Tag 057G, lemma-slice-smooth, proof, entire case d = 0; existing etale-neighbourhood criterion packages its first shrinking, and Tag 02GL with Tag 01K1 gives the final isolation.
